description: NASA's forgotten equipment on the Moon and Mars holds untold stories. Our team combines AI, storytelling, design, software development, 3D experiences, and data visualization to create an engaging digital experience that brings these historical artifacts back to life. We're looking for developers, designers, storytellers, artists, data specialists, and space enthusiasts who want to build something impactful, creative, and innovative together.
summary: SILENT FLEET, this project turns spacecraft and exploration equipment left on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space into an interactive, scroll-driven story. Visitors travel through a WebGL-rendered 3D continuum, explore a coordinate-based atlas and archive, and open mission dossiers with locations, context, images, and source links. Dossiers distinguish sourced mission information from creative monologues; the monologues are not archival recordings. The project aims to make mission history and science more engaging to explore. It is an educational prototype; measured reach, learning outcomes, and independent scientific validation are not documented.
details:
Silent Fleet is a single-page React experience. Scrolling moves through Moon, transit, Mars, storm, and deep-space scenes rendered with Three.js and React Three Fiber. Visitors can explore a coordinate-based atlas, filter a mission archive, and open dossiers with mission context, coordinates, imagery, and citations. Creative monologues are explicitly labeled as fiction, not archival recordings.

The project makes mission history explorable by connecting a visual location to source-linked mission information. It uses NASA imagery and credits the Voyager 3D model to NASA VTAD. Moon and Mars textures are Solar System Scope / INOVE visual maps under CC BY 4.0; their attribution notes tuned colors and fictional terrain in unmapped areas, so they are not primary scientific datasets. Mission records are stored in a static catalog; the app does not use a live NASA data API or perform scientific analysis.

The intended benefit is educational storytelling; no user testing or measured learning impact is documented. The app uses React 19, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber/Drei, GSAP/ScrollTrigger, Lenis, Framer Motion, Web Audio, and browser speech synthesis. Audio is optional. A public deployment and independent scientific validation are not documented.
